Title: CLO x DAZ3D Avatar Development Guide
PDF_Text: STEPS TO TRANSLATE FROM DAZ TO CLO CLO x DAZ3D AVATAR DEVELOPMENT 1. Export Settings from Daz3D 2. Editing Textures in Photoshop 3. Applying Textures 4. Overlay Colors in CLO 5. Opacity and Reﬂection in CLO 6. Posing 7. Studio Lighting 8. Render Settings 9. Save CONTENTS Recommended Export Settings FBX 2010Binary (this version of FBX will export a rig and skinning compatible with CLO) Merge Diffuse and Opacity Textures (this will export the appropriate patterns like hair and lashes with no background) Merge Clothing into Figure Skeleton (this will keep shoes, hair etc attached to the body) Export Avatar in A pose Example Rig DAZ3D EXPORT SETTINGS Avatar Styling Fig. 1. Default Levels Fig. 2. Change Value from 1 to .45 Fig. 3. Change Saturation Fig. 4. Overlay a Color on the White Hair Texture Gamma Correction (Follow this link to Understand Gamma Correction and refer to Fig.2.) Reduce Saturation of Image (Generally after Gamma Correction, the textures will become oversaturated. Change saturation value between -20 and -30) Use your artistic freedom, change skin tone, make up, etc as you please. Eg. If you have .pngs of the blush, you can layer them here. You can make the skin tone more cold or warm as per your liking. You can paint on blush, eyeliner, brows, lipstick, etc. Change Hair and Lash Color in Photoshop (Overlay the desired hair color in Photoshop on the desaturated hair textures) EDIT TEXTURES IN PHOTOSHOP Fig. 1. Eye Texture EXCEPTIONS TO TEXTURES APPLICATION Overwrite the ﬁles in the original folder and save .psd ﬁles in a seperate folder. Simply Refresh Textures (F5) in CLO to see the edited outcome without manually applying the edited textures. There will be no textures on the outer layer of the eyeball. Textures are on a layer inside. (Refer Fig.1.) COLOR OVERLAYING Remove Textures from Micro hairs and add the hair color in CLO if you want them to render visibly. Overlay Colors on hair, skin, lips, nails, shoes, etc, to get a more desirable effect. As V-Ray and I-Ray render differently and Daz has shaders that CLO doesnt, this may be a necessary step depending on how speciﬁc you are about the output as well as from a styling perspective. These settings will be saved in your .avt ﬁle. Make eyebrows and lashes darker than rest of the hair for a natural look. Texture & Color Tip: You can use the Scene Tab in the Object Browser to ﬁnd small or layered parts of your Avatar, eg, hair, lashes and eyes to change their texture, color or pose. Apply Glass Material Type to outer white layer of eyes. Apply Normal Map to Lips. Apply Reﬂection Silk/Satin Material Type to Hair Apply Reﬂection settings to skin according to desired effect. Apply Plastic, Metal or Leather effects Material Types to any Accessories like shoes, etc. Opacity and Reﬂection Presentation & Output Eye Pose edited in CLO Body Pose edited in CLO POSING To bring Poses from Daz, export a .fbx with the desired pose with no textures (make sure all other settings are same) Import in CLO Save As > Pose Open > Pose in desired Project File Create Poses in CLO using the Rig Youcanchangedirectionoftheeyes,changethe expressions,etc. LIGHTING Use High Contrast Lighting Studio Add any additional lighting as per your aesthetic Presentation Depth of Field Off Depth of Field On RENDER SETTINGS Depth of Field. Background objects will be blurred giving a more real life photoshoot effect. Also a neat trick to soften edges of hair mesh. Ground Shadow High Contrast Studio Lighting Preset SAVE After getting the desired output your avatar can be saved as an .avt ﬁle and it will retain all changes made in and outside of CLO. Render & Save All Rights Reserved FINAL RENDERINGS Time Taken: Approximately 2 hours Thank You!
PDF_Summary: Comprehensive Guide to Translating from Daz to Clo Clo x Daz3D Avatar Development: Step 1: Export Settings from Daz3D - Recommended export settings: - FBX 2010 Binary format (compatible with CLO) - Merge diffuse and opacity textures (for appropriate patterns like hair and lashes) - Merge clothing into figure skeleton (to keep attached accessories) - Export avatar in A pose - Example rig: Daz3D Export Settings Avatar Styling Step 2: Editing Textures in Photoshop - Open textures in Photoshop - Make desired changes to skin tone, makeup, etc. - Overlay hair and lash colors on desaturated hair textures Step 3: Applying Textures - Overwrite the files in the original folder with edited textures - Save .psd files in a separate folder for backup - Refresh textures (F5) in CLO to see the edited outcome without manually applying textures - Note: No textures on the outer layer of the eyeball, textures are on a layer inside Step 4: Overlay Colors in CLO - Remove textures from micro hairs and add hair color in CLO for visible rendering - Overlay colors on hair, skin, lips, nails, shoes, etc. for desired effect - This step may be necessary for specific output and styling, considering differences in rendering engines and shaders Step 5: Opacity and Reflection in CLO - Apply glass material type to outer white layer of eyes - Apply normal map to lips - Apply reflection silk/satin material type to hair - Adjust reflection settings on skin for desired effect - Apply plastic, metal, or leather effects material types to accessories like shoes Step 6: Posing - To bring poses from Daz, export a .fbx file with desired pose and no textures - Import the file in CLO - Save it as a pose and open it in the desired project file - Create poses in CLO using the rig - Adjust eye direction, expressions, etc. Step 7: Studio Lighting - Use high contrast lighting studio - Add additional lighting as per aesthetic preference Step 8: Render Settings - Use depth of field for a more realistic photoshoot effect - Adjust ground shadow and contrast studio lighting preset Step 9: Save - Save the avatar as an .avt file to retain all changes made in and outside of CLO Note: This guide assumes all rights are reserved for the final renderings. The process may take approximately 2 hours. Thank you for using this comprehensive guide for translating from Daz to Clo Clo x Daz3D Avatar Development.
